Maps the changes to Well-Architected pillars: dropping sticky sessions and session stores, header-based routing, W3C trace context, idempotent tools, protocol-declared caching, and security requirements like HMAC-protected continuation tokens and ownership checks. Includes migration advice for keeping legacy session infrastructure until old clients are gone.
title: MCP went stateless: Is your AWS MCP server deployment well-architected?

summary: Part 1 of an AWS series describing an architecture for centrally orchestrating bare-metal servers and EKS Anywhere clusters across many on-premises sites, using Lambda, Step Functions, EventBridge and DynamoDB. It covers the inventory/state model (sites, servers, clusters, orders), the Step Functions callback pattern for long-running on-prem tasks, Distributed Map for fan-out, Redfish for vendor-agnostic hardware control, and hybrid security setup.
title: Hybrid cloud orchestration: Modernizing on-premises infrastructure management with AWS

summary: Describes a graduated-autonomy architecture for AI agents where permissions expand or contract based on a rolling trust score, with safety as an independent floor and hysteresis between tiers. Covers pre-execution checks, out-of-process Cedar policy enforcement via a gateway, audit/provenance records, eval-gated delivery, honeypot monitoring, and delegation-chain minimum tiers. AWS-specific services are used but the pattern is broadly transferable.
title: Closing the AI agent trust gap with graduated autonomy

summary: Based on interviews with about 20 engineering leaders, the article explains why CTOs and VPs of Engineering are quitting or taking career breaks in 2026. Reasons include founders with unrealistic AI expectations, cost-cutting pressure, equity wiped out by liquidation preferences, and smaller teams needing fewer leaders. It also walks through how preference stacks can make a 2% equity grant worthless, and how the market now favors AI-native leadership experience.
title: Headed for the Exit: the Great Engineering Leader Career Break

summary: Jim Highsmith proposes 'Practitioner Voice' as a writing category distinct from academic writing, thought leadership, and LLM-generated prose. It is characterized by authority from experience, tensions left unresolved, a visible author, and readers who recognize the pattern from their own work. Useful for engineers who write design docs, blog posts, or technical essays and want their writing to carry real judgment.
title: Practitioner Voice: The Writing Category Nobody has Named Yet

summary: Podcast episode notes with Addy Osmani covering his path from Chrome DevTools and Core Web Vitals to AI developer experience at Google. Key takeaways include the risk of 'cognitive surrender' when working with AI agents, 'mutual amplification' and loop engineering practices, accountability as the enduring role of engineers, and career advice about broadening into product and go-to-market skills.
title: From Chrome DevTools to AI Engineering, with Addy Osmani

summary: Describes Gallup's production RAG assistant on AWS: dual retrieval from Bedrock Knowledge Bases and Kendra with confidence-threshold filtering, Lambda/FastAPI streaming, ElastiCache for conversation history with RDS as system of record, and token/latency metrics via Firehose. Includes details like persisting interactions before streaming and mid-stream guardrail intervention, but is largely a vendor case study with limited depth.
title: Gallup scales real-time coaching for thousands with Amazon Bedrock

summary: Explores why netip.AddrFrom16(ip.As16()) is about 8x slower than a native IPv4-to-IPv6 mapping method in Go, comparing stdlib, helper, and unsafe implementations with benchmarks and generated assembly. It then walks through the Go compiler's phases and IR dumps to patch the noder and optimize the pack/copy/unpack pattern.
title: Hacking the Go compiler to efficiently map IPv4 to IPv6

summary: A collection of short notes from Martin Fowler. The main thread argues that higher-level code still matters when LLMs write software, drawing on Sam Ruby's example that a Rails app of about 60K tokens grows to about 4M tokens in C, and on Unmesh Joshi's view of code as a conceptual model. Other notes cover the move from deterministic building to 'nurturing' inferential systems, an Evans/Fowler interview on AI, and hallucination-rate trade-offs between models.
title: Fragments: October 4

summary: Analyzes 150 production incidents in compound AI systems (RAG, tool-using, orchestrated LLM pipelines) to build a taxonomy of 23 failure modes across retrieval, generation, tool, orchestration, and integration categories. It proposes resilience patterns such as circuit breakers, output quality gates, and component isolation, and measures their effectiveness with fault injection experiments. Only the abstract is shown here, so the depth of the full paper is unverified.
title: Compound AI System Reliability: A Failure Taxonomy and Resilience Pattern Catalog from 150 Production Incidents

summary: A postmortem of a data pipeline bug where a non-unique cache key silently dropped 99.9% of records while jobs reported success. The author draws out three habits: row-conservation accounting with ratio floors at every stage boundary, idempotent reruns via deterministic natural keys, upserts and database unique constraints, and SCD Type 2 dimensions that use null-safe change detection.
title: A cache key ate 99.9% of my records and the pipeline looked green

summary: Walks through the four-phase zero-downtime migration playbook (dual-write, backfill, verify, cut over) with Python code for a phase-aware router, keyset-cursor backfill, and continuous sampling verification. Explains specific failure modes: backfilling before dual-write, stale backfill overwriting fresh writes, shadow-write failures coupling availability, and noisy verification. It also covers the harder edge cases: cross-store transactions, schema changes mid-migration, and non-key-value reads.
title: Zero-Downtime Database Migration: The Dual-Write Window Is Where It Goes Wrong

summary: Models an online feature store as a materialized view over an event stream and defines a per-feature freshness budget, proving a staleness bound and a closed-form threshold below which a feature can never be served in budget. Validates this in simulation and on a Kafka/Redis/PostgreSQL pipeline, and shows that phase-locked request and recomputation clocks in simulations systematically under-observe staleness.
title: Feature Freshness Budgets for Real-Time ML Inference Under Stream Lag

summary: Presents LOGOS, an unsupervised system that uses entity-event co-occurrence and temporal precedence to compress millions of raw, unannotated log lines into a compact precedence forest that shows how a failure propagated. It is evaluated on 25 enterprise outages and 12 open-source issues, where it removes about 99.8% of noise and consolidates alert floods 124x. Feeding its output to an LLM gave 80% (enterprise) and 100% (open-source) zero-shot root-cause accuracy.
title: From Alert Floods to Precedence Forests: Zero-Prior-Knowledge Incident Triage with LOGOS

summary: Presents Beaver, a system for co-locating latency-critical vRAN processing with best-effort ML workloads on a shared GPU. It resizes SM partitions at slot granularity based on scheduled work, and rewrites ML kernels so they yield HBM bandwidth during the vRAN's memory-critical phases. On an H200 it keeps p99.9 latency within a 1.5ms deadline while retaining 74% of Llama-3.3-70B serving throughput.
title: Beaver: Elastic GPU Sharing between ML and Latency-Critical vRAN Workloads

summary: Shows how to enable Podman's Docker-compatible API socket as a rootless user via systemd and point DOCKER_HOST at it so docker-compose and the docker CLI work unchanged. Also covers user namespaces, podman unshare/mount for inspecting container files, rootless Docker as an alternative, and user lingering to keep containers running after logout.
title: Using docker-compose with Podman rootless

summary: Practical lessons from running a Laravel SaaS with a database per tenant across 2,000+ customers. Covers initializing tenancy in queued jobs, tenant-prefixing cache keys, adding a business sub-scope within tenants, keeping migrations idempotent across N databases, rolling-forward settings defaults, and a checklist for testing isolation.
title: Database-per-tenant in Laravel: 6 lessons from running a multi-tenant SaaS
